Thomas Carlyle, Sartor Resartus.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/thomas-carlyle/sartor-resartus

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Thomas Carlyle (annotator, author), died 1881.

First publication of the text used (SE colophon: 'Sartor Resartus was published between 1833 and 1834 by Thomas Carlyle.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published before 1931 (SE colophon: 'Sartor Resartus was published between 1833 and 1834 by Thomas Carlyle.'), so it is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement below says the same.
- Country of origin: does not matter, because every person whose words are in the text died in 1925 or earlier. The text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The last person to die died in 1881.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
